title: The Between Moment
question: I stand between was and will-be, belonging to neither; philosophers chase me but never catch me still. What am I?
hintText:
Was trails behind where I stand.
Will-be waits just ahead always.
Chasers never catch me resting.
correctExplanation: The present — between was and will-be, belonging to neither. Chase ensures escape.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the present. Was-behind plus will-ahead isolates now: belonging to neither neighbor. Chasing moves the quarry.
lessonContent:
Chasing moves quarry reliably here.
Neighbors flank what belongs nowhere.
Was trails; will waits constantly.
Stillness escapes all pursuit.
Share this: stand between moments.

title: The Painless Cut
question: Barbers sever me daily without a wince from owners; what grows from roots feels nothing at the ends. What am I?
hintText:
Barbers sever me painlessly daily.
Roots grow what ends never feel.
Owners wince at bills, never cuts.
correctExplanation: Hair — dead tissue cut painlessly: roots live, ends don't. Severing without suffering.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is hair. Cut-without-wince plus grow-from-roots isolates dead keratin: living follicles, lifeless lengths. Barbers harvest painlessly.
lessonContent:
Living roots feed lifeless lengths.
Harvests painlessly repeat daily.
Dead tissue serves living heads.
Severing spares feeling fully.
Share this: cut painlessly once.

title: The Starved Feast
question: Misers hoard me, monks renounce me, yet I grow by giving, not getting. Advertisers manufacture me nightly. What am I?
hintText:

Giving grows what getting starves.

correctExplanation: Desire — hoarded by misers, renounced by monks, grown by giving. Manufactured nightly, satisfied never.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is desire. Hoard-renounce plus grow-by-giving isolates wanting: advertisers farm it, monks fallow it. Starved feasts feed on lack.
lessonContent:
Advertisers farm nightly harvests.
Giving grows what getting starves.
Monks fallow fertile wants.
Starved feasts feed on lack.
Share this: fast one want today.

Avoided arrivals mock workers.

title: The Same Opposite

correctExplanation: Inflammable — opposite-prefixed, identically meaning. Negation failed on spelling.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is inflammable. Opposite-means-same isolates contranyms of prefix: in- negates nothing here. Fire obeys both spellings.
lessonContent:
Opposite prefixes match meanings.
Fire obeys both forms alike.
Negation failed on this spelling.
Same sense wears contrary coats.

title: The Unanswerable Yes

hintText:

Sleepers cannot testify truly.
Only no answers honestly.
correctExplanation: Are you asleep — yes falsifies itself: sleepers can't testify, liars can only say no. Questions defeating answers.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is are you asleep. Truthful yeses impossible: sleep precludes testifying, waking falsifies content. Self-defeating questions guard paradoxes.
lessonContent:
Yes answers falsify themselves here.
Truth demands negative replies.
Sleepers never testify truly.
Unanswerable yeses guard paradoxes.
